back: The series of activities and phases a project passes through from start to closure.
Logically related activities ending in one or more deliverables or outcomes. Sequential, transitional or overlapping.
Continue; continue with modification; end; remain; repeat the phase or part of it; park the project temporarily.

front: Risk and cost of change over time
back: Risk and uncertainty fall; the cost of changes rises; cheap influence on scope is highest at the start.
The means used to create and evolve the product: predictive, adaptive or hybrid. Not the same as a development phase.
Scope stable early; big investment or regulation; iterating costs more than it is worth (construction build).
Scope planned up front, delivered in parts; earlier value, but overall scope and timeline largely fixed.
Uncertain, volatile requirements; design and new product development; evolving digital projects.
Iterative: refine through repeated cycles. Incremental: deliver in small usable segments that build on each other.
Generally 1 to 4 weeks, with a demonstration at the end of each.
A method is a systematic way of doing something; a tool kit offers options to choose from. Disciplined Agile is a tool kit.
Most projects can strongly benefit from a hybrid approach: flexibility plus control over predictable parts.
Adaptive then predictive rollout; both simultaneously; mostly predictive with an adaptive part; mostly adaptive with a predictive part.
Requirements uncertainty against technical uncertainty. Both certain: predictive. More uncertain: adaptive or exploratory.
Simple, complicated, complex, chaotic, disorder. Complex: probe, sense, respond.
Deliverables, project, organization.
Known requirements, costly change, rigorous safety requirements, significant regulation.
Innovation, unstable scope, risk and uncertainty, value from frequent feedback, deliverable in parts.
Hierarchical, directing culture: predictive. Network structure, self-managed teams: adaptive. Some frameworks: three to nine members.
A decision-making tool (not a rigid procedure) that evaluates culture, team and project to choose the initial approach.
Single, multiple, periodic (regular fixed schedule), continuous (production-ready increments all the time).
The deliberate adaptation of the approach, governance and processes to the project's environment and objectives.
Too few processes: ineffective. Too many: costly and wasteful. Benefits: team commitment, customer focus, efficient resources.
Add, modify, remove, blend, align.
Select the approach; tailor for the organization; tailor for the project; implement ongoing improvement.
